summary: Hosted service, sprint 1z: the server runs on your own machine. `pnpm self-hosted:up` starts the same API, worker, page fetcher, Postgres and web screen as the cloud with Docker Compose (deploy/local/compose.yaml), with random secrets generated at first start and the web screen on 127.0.0.1 only. A self-hosted stack takes its Claude and OpenAI keys from files, runs the `direct` model routes with prompt caching, and keeps uploads and exports on disk under the same tenant keys as Cloud Storage. A deployment can also offer local models on an OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as Ollama, as the writer or the reviewer, with a warning in the start dialog and the model setup while a local model writes the CV. Injection screening with Claude works on the direct route too. The cloud deployment is unchanged: it keeps Claude on Vertex AI in the EU, keys in Secret Manager and files in Cloud Storage. See docs/operations/self-hosted.md.
knownLimitations: Staging only: production keeps its earlier images until the owner deploys this tag there, and staging itself does not use the new self-hosted settings. A self-hosted stack has one workspace behind the owner token, no sign-in and plain HTTP, so it is for one person's machine only. With your own keys, Claude and OpenAI process material outside the EU under your provider terms. Local models are unpriced and have not passed the quality check. The cost of a complete cached run is still to measure (#1597).
